opening.text:
Dozens of candles light a circular altar. Several bodies lie on the floor, marked with strange symbols. An old priest stands with his back to the entrance.
"You are late."
He draws a sign in the air.
"I expected you sooner."
Slowly he turns around.
"Well then. Perhaps our guest at least has the courtesy to give his name."

choices.text: "I'm here to put an end to this madness."
"You are Vaelor. The man who slaughters people for his rituals."
"Kneel, old man. Maybe I'll let you live."
"You should find yourself a better religion. This one doesn't seem to work very well." [Provoke]
"I want to understand what you are trying to do here."
(Step back and leave him for now.)

philosophy.text:
"Madness?"
He laughs softly.
"You have no idea what is happening here. And yet you are already willing to kill people for it."

"Tell me, stranger."
"How many people have you seen die?"
"How many have you killed yourself?"

choices.text: "I don't care. Dying is part of living."
"You hide behind your religion because you are a cowardly murderer." [Provoke]
"You really believe you can bring back the dead?"

sacrifice.text:
"Slaughters?"
He looks at one of the bodies.
"How crude."
"I prefer the word offering."

"Every step forward demands sacrifice."
"Kingdoms were built on corpses. Wars are fought for a handful of land."
"And you condemn me because I sacrifice seven lives to save thousands?"

choices.text: "If seven people are necessary, why not sacrifice yourself?"
"Seven people? Then an eighth won't bother you." [Provoke]

hesitates.text:
Vaelor studies you in silence.
"Interesting. You have killed before."
"But have you ever watched someone you loved die?"
Vaelor hesitates.

pathetic.text:
"You threaten a man who has already looked death in the face."
"How utterly pathetic."

"Tell me, stranger."
"How many people have you seen die?"
"How many have you killed yourself?"

faith.text:
"Mock all you like."
"Your gods have abandoned people just as mine have."

"The gods are silent."
"My wife begged to be healed. My son fasted forty days for her."
"She died anyway."

choices.text: "Perhaps it was the will of your gods." [Provoke]
"Your wife would never have wanted these murders."
"You lost your wife and decided others should suffer the same."

understand.text:
"Understand?"
For the first time the priest shows real interest.
"Perhaps you are not just another armed fool after all."

"Something lies beneath this city."
"Something older than our kingdoms."
"I have heard its voice."

choices.text: "You are mad. There is no voice."
"Show me the source of your power."
"What happens when you finish the ritual?"

judge.text: "No. You want to judge. That is something else entirely."

"A pretty lie."
"Death does not care about justice."

phil_comfortable.text: "A remarkably comfortable view for someone who still breathes."

phil_necessary.text:
"Ah."
He smiles.
"Then perhaps we are less different than you think."

phil_careful.text:
"Careful."
The candles begin to flicker.
"I am ready to sacrifice myself for my faith. Are you ready to die for yours?"

phil_know.text:

"I know it is possible."

sacr_yes.text:
"Yes."
He says it completely calmly.
"And I will not forget their faces until the day I die."

sacr_trembles.text: Vaelor's hands tremble slightly. He truly suffers under what he has done, but he justifies his guilt with fanatical conviction.

choices.text: "You know this is wrong. You are only afraid to admit it."

sacr_unsure.text:
Vaelor is silent for an unusually long time.
"Because... someone has to complete the ceremony."
For the first time he sounds unsure.

Vaelor looks at his burned hand.
"I promised them their sacrifice would not be in vain."
"If I stop now..."
His voice breaks.
"Then I killed them for nothing."

choices.text: "Then at least stop anyone else from dying."
"You are a monster. But you can still give yourself up."
"Finish the ritual. I want to see whether you are right."
"Your wife is dead. And you are about to follow her." [Provoke]

sacr_dead_man.text: "Because a dead man cannot perform rituals."

sacr_eighth.text:

"You will find that I am not as helpless as my victims."

"But then explain to me why the dead sometimes whisper my name."

rese_records.text:

"Not as ghosts. As living, breathing people."

rese_stone.text:

"There. It answers, sometimes."
You have found the weak point of the ritual.

lyra.text: Good. A living fanatic is far more useful than a dead one.

seren.text: Tie him up properly. Men like that regret their deeds remarkably fast once they smell an advantage.
